messages.author: 061281a8cdc1f42e
messages.subject: Access "cov.lv" from fit object
parts:
Hello,
 
I'm running a multiple group factor analysis and I'm getting the error that I have non-positive definite latent covariance matrix and that I should use inspect(fit, "cov.lv") for further information. This works well to see the model implied covariance matrix, but I'd like to be able to take that one step further and see whether its positive definition. For right now, I've just been re-creating this values in a new matrix and then using the det() command, but is there a way I can access the cov.lv information from the fit object? Ideally, I'd like to be able to directly submit each group's covariance matrix to the det() command instead of having to re-create it. Thank you.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Access "cov.lv" from fit object
parts:
With a multiple group model, inspect(fit, "cov.lv") returns a list with a covariance matrix for each group. So use the det() function with each element in the list:

#First group
det(inspect(fit, "cov.lv)[[1]])

#Second group
det(inspect(fit, "cov.lv)[[2]])

#And so on...

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Access "cov.lv" from fit object
parts:
On 11/14/2013 11:38 PM, Alex Schoemann wrote:
> With a multiple group model, inspect(fit, "cov.lv") returns a list with
> a covariance matrix for each group.

To replicate the test done by lavaan (ie to test if the covariance
matrices are positive definite), you must compute the eigenvalues:

lapply(inspect(fit, "cov.lv"), eigen, only.values=TRUE, symmetric=TRUE)

The eigenvalues should all be strictly positive, although lavaan 0.5-14
has relaxed this a little bit by using a 'tolerance' (ie we allow for
some tiny tiny negative values). After a lot of tinkering, this is what
we now use (assuming the eigenvalues are in eigvals):

any(eigvals < -1 * .Machine$double.eps^(3/4))

if this returns true, you get the warning.

It is also often interesting to look at the correlations (instead of the
covariances):

inspect(fit, "cor.lv")

Yves.
